facts.value: The Classical republican concept of 'civil society' dates back to Hobbes and Locke.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Locke saw civil society as people who have 'a common established law and judicature to appeal to, with authority to decide controversies between them.'
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel distinguished the 'state' from 'civil society' in Elements of the Philosophy of Right.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Hegel believed that civil society and the state were opposites, within the scheme of his dialectic theory of history.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: In post-modern theory, civil society is necessarily a source of law, by being the basis from which people form opinions and lobby for what they believe law should be.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: One of its primary modern sources is found in the responses of ordinary men and women, and of the non-governmental organizations which many of them support, to the human rights abuses they see on the television screen in their living rooms.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Freedom of speech, freedom of association and many other individual rights allow people to gather, discuss, criticise and hold to account their governments, from which the basis of a deliberative democracy is formed.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The more people are involved with, concerned by, and capable of changing how political power is exercised over their lives, the more acceptable and legitimate the law becomes to the people.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The most familiar institutions of civil society include economic markets, profit-oriented firms, families, trade unions, hospitals, universities, schools, charities, debating clubs, non-governmental organisations, neighbourhoods, churches, and religious associations.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: There is no clear legal definition of civil society, and of the institutions it includes.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Most institutions and bodies that compile lists of institutions exclude political parties.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA
